name: Freeport-McMoRan Inc.

profile.description: Freeport-McMoRan is the world's largest publicly traded copper producer, operating the Grasberg minerals district in Indonesia (FCX holds 48.76% of PT Freeport Indonesia), mines in Arizona, New Mexico and Colorado, and Cerro Verde (Peru) and El Abra (Chile). It produces copper, gold and molybdenum. Q3 2026 attributable net income was ~$1.2B ($0.81 per share; $0.88 adjusted) on ~830M lbs of copper production and realized copper above $6.50/lb. Grasberg mill throughput is ~67% of pre-incident rates after the September 2025 mud rush, with 80% capacity targeted by mid-2027 and near-full capacity by end-2027. CEO Kathleen Quirk has led the company since June 2024. Headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona; market cap ~$90B.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Freeport's leaching innovation program, which applies new technologies, data analytics and an internally developed additive tested at Morenci, produced 214M lbs of incremental copper in 2025 and 101M lbs in H1 2026, and targets a 300M lb annual run rate by year-end 2026. That is effectively a new low-cost mine without greenfield capex [4][5]. AI Deployment (1/2): The leaching program relies on data analytics and new applications, but Freeport does not explicitly quantify AI-driven results [4]. Market Share (2/2): Freeport is the world's largest publicly traded copper producer, producing ~830M lbs of copper per quarter [1][2]. Pipeline (2/2): The pipeline has specific milestones: Grasberg at 80% capacity by mid-2027 and near-full by end-2027, the Production Block 1S restart in mid-2027, the PTFI smelter restart (late August 2026), and a decision by year-end 2026 on doubling capacity at Bagdad [2][3]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Freeport reports no separate R&D expense, typical for mining [6].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Freeport's 'Accelerate the Future, Responsibly' framing connects copper to electrification, but it reads as strategy rather than a distinctive purpose. The September 2025 Grasberg mud rush, which killed seven workers, tests the 'responsibly' claim [7]. Community Impact (0/2): Our research found no quantified community-investment figures, so this item scores 0. Employee Retention (1/2): Leadership continuity is strong. Quirk spent decades as CFO and President before succeeding Richard Adkerson, which reflects a deep internal bench, but no company-wide turnover data was found [5]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP Form 4 data show zero open-market insider purchases in 2025-2026 against 5 sales in Q3 2026 and 7 in Q1 2026 (about 0.92M shares disposed), which is net selling [8].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Scored mechanically on the Growth-sleeve metrics. Every metric except profit margin reaches its target: D/E of 30.8%, ROE of 15.7% (2x weight), a 5-year revenue CAGR of 13.2% (FY2020 $13.9B to FY2025 $25.7B; 2x weight), forward P/E of 14.4 and a forward PEG of 0.25 (FMP; 2x weight), the last reflecting expected earnings growth as Grasberg ramps and copper prices exceed $6.50/lb [1][6][9]. TTM revenue growth of 8.2% is near the 10% target. Net margin of 13.0% is the only real weakness, reflecting the Indonesian government's majority interest in PTFI earnings [3]. Raw weighted score 9.59, which rounds to 10. Liquidity is about $769M of daily traded value.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Copper mining, concentrating and smelting are physical operations that AI cannot substitute. Data-center buildout for AI applications adds to copper demand for power distribution and cooling infrastructure, so AI is a demand tailwind rather than a threat [1][10]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Freeport does not disclose AI-specific revenue. Its benefit from AI-driven demand is indirect, through copper prices, so the tiebreaker point is not awarded.

infinite_game.summary: Freeport plays a long game in a cyclical industry. It has committed to multi-decade assets (the Grasberg block-cave conversion and an extension of operating rights beyond 2041), exited oil and gas to refocus on copper, and pursues a technology-first leaching strategy that Quirk argues the industry should prefer over exploration. The fatal 2025 mud rush and Grasberg's environmental legacy temper Sinek's assessment, as does the absence of evidence that Freeport treats rivals as benchmarks.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Supplying the copper that electrification and digital infrastructure require is a genuine cause, and it shapes long-dated decisions such as the Grasberg permit extension beyond 2041 and the Bagdad expansion study [2][3]. The seven fatalities in the 2025 mud rush and a long-running tailings controversy at Grasberg keep the cause from being fully validated [3][7].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Quirk has publicly argued that miners should shift investment from exploration to technology, and she has backed that view with an internally developed leaching program targeting a 300M lb annual run rate [4][5]. Freeport also continued the multi-year Grasberg recovery and smelter restart rather than retrenching [2]. This is meaningful courage, though partly forced by circumstance.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The planned succession from Adkerson to Quirk preserved institutional continuity [5]. The 2025 mud rush, however, raises questions about safety culture at Grasberg, and no standout employee-trust data was found [7].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): Freeport exited the oil and gas business it acquired in 2013 to refocus on copper, converted Grasberg from open-pit to underground block-cave mining (extending the asset's life by decades), and is now redefining growth around leaching technology rather than new mines [4][5][6].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Our research found no management commentary framing BHP, Southern Copper or other peers as rivals that push Freeport to improve. Its communications focus on its own scale and assets [1][5].

investment_thesis: Freeport combines the strongest mechanical financials in its peer set (Infrastructure 10/10: D/E 31%, ROE 16%, forward P/E 14, forward PEG 0.25) with direct exposure to structural copper demand from electrification and AI data centers [6][9][10]. Q3 2026 earnings of $0.88 adjusted per share on realized copper above $6.50/lb show that the cash engine is intact while Grasberg recovers [1][2].
thesis_continued: The upside depends on the Grasberg ramp (67% of pre-incident throughput today, 80% by mid-2027, near-full by end-2027), the scale-up of leaching to a 300M lb run rate, and the Bagdad doubling decision [2][4]. The stock has fallen from ~$80 to ~$62 on ramp-up delay concerns, and Indonesian officials have suggested full recovery could slip to 2028 [3][11]. Weak Inspiration evidence (net insider selling, safety legacy) keeps Freeport at HOLD rather than BUY.
key_catalysts: Grasberg ramp to 80% capacity by mid-2027 and Production Block 1S restart [2]
Leaching initiative scaling to a 300M lb annual run rate by year-end 2026 [4]
Year-end 2026 decision on doubling Bagdad (Arizona) capacity [2]
Copper prices above $6.50/lb on electrification and AI data-center demand [1][10]
key_risks: Further Grasberg recovery delays (Indonesian officials have floated 2028) [3][11]
Safety and environmental liabilities following the 2025 mud rush (seven fatalities) [7]
Indonesian sovereign and ownership risk (PTFI 51.24% government-held) [3]
Copper price cyclicality and U.S. operating disruptions (flooding, power outages) [2]
